title: Change tier
summary: The Change tier dialog opened from the tier control on licenses.detail: moving Priya Raman's automatic Education license up to Studio (every changed limit with now and after, what stays, and why the move sticks), and down to Free, where a warning says her next sign-in moves it back to Education because an Access rule still covers her.
compare: It opens from three places on the license record: the tier control top-right (Tier Education ▾), Change tier… in the ⋯ menu, and the Limits card. Title: 'Change <holder>'s tier'.
'Move to' is one select of the product's tiers with each one's rank (1 of 5) and a one-line summary of the chosen tier; the hint names the current tier and its rank.

'What changes' lists only the fields that change, each with now → after and the source of the new value (Devices: '10 from Studio + 2 from seat pack'); Duration is recomputed from the new tier (Fixed, ends Sep 14, 2027 → Lifetime).
A 'Stays' line names what the move keeps: values set on the license (offline days 14), unchanged limits and every add-on.
Moving up an automatic license: it stays an Automatic grant and the dialog says sign-ins only move licenses up, so the move sticks.

Moving down while an Access rule still covers the holder: a warning callout says the next sign-in moves it back up, names the rule (Verified email domain example.edu gives Education) and offers Open Access; the move is not blocked. Lower values are in the warning tone, and a device count that drops below the devices in use says how many get signed out.
Buttons: Cancel and 'Move to <tier>' (primary). No 'Save' or 'Confirm'. After it, a toast 'Moved to Studio' and the Limits card shows the new sources.
Phone: a bottom sheet (the kit's .sheet); each row puts the field name over now → after; the buttons stack, primary on top.
